completed_stage_receipts.summary: Confirmed a control-plane state-drift defect: the user explicitly reports deleting the Continuity monitors and current product-state reread shows the declared core monitor tasks absent, while durable/rebuildable repository surfaces still claim them enabled or hourly-active. The user deletion is intentional product mutation; the defect is stale repository liveness representation, not the deletion itself.

Classified the failure as external-product-observation-staleness: mutable ChatGPT automation state can change outside repository writes, so a past enabled observation cannot remain represented as current liveness truth. User intent to delete must not be auto-reversed.

Mapped the affected path: live ChatGPT automation product state -> monitor liveness observation -> rebuildable HARNESS_STATUS -> authoritative maintenance manifest/handoff summary -> future maintenance decisions. Bypass surface is any external product mutation that does not also write GitHub. BUSINESS owner state and leases are out of scope.

Prior mitigation used peer liveness checks but explicitly could not detect simultaneous loss of all monitors. This new user-initiated all-monitor deletion is a known-class recurrence at the product/repository boundary. Escalation therefore moves above peer-watch repair to the state-authority model: repository may retain expectation/last-observed evidence, but current product liveness must require fresh product re-observation and must never be inferred from a stale durable flag.

Satisfied the learning scout from current first-party product-state observation, the user correction, the prior liveness incident and current internal authorities. External browsing is not decision-relevant because the defect is a freshness/authority mismatch and the decisive current fact is available from the connected product surface.
Reused the existing automation-state read, task manifest/handoff, rebuildable HARNESS_STATUS and signal/issue path. Rejected a new watchdog, registry, policy or permanent Agent.

Rejected auto-recreating monitors because it would override explicit user intent; rejected persisting DELETED as timeless truth because it can stale again; accepted separating durable policy from timestamped last-observed product state and requiring live reread for present-tense liveness claims.

Resolved retrievable facts autonomously. User intent is known: deletion was intentional. Whether monitors should be recreated later remains a genuine future user/product decision and is not inferred by this maintenance run.

No account/startup instruction change is required. The defect occurs after repository bootstrap and must be repaired in repository state semantics; more prompt text would not make external scheduler observations fresh.

Designed a zero-new-authority repair: current liveness decisions require live product reread; repository stores desired semantics plus timestamped last observation/provenance only. No new Agent/task/registry/root policy and no business hot-path preload are added.

Architecture payoff is removal of false present-tense liveness claims after out-of-band product mutations. The repair demotes persistent ENABLED/hourly flags from current truth to historical observation and adds no parallel mechanism.
